claims.statement: ParamBinding (services/ParamBinding.h, port of useParameter.ts) is a view's handle on one host parameter, values normalised 0..1. It brackets drag writes in beginGesture/dragTo/endGesture so the host records one automation gesture, and inbound parameter echoes are ignored while the pointer is down (a stale echo must not snap the live value back). Change notifications fire on the message thread; an unknown id (a build without that parameter) yields an inert binding that reads 0 and swallows writes, so views never null-check.

MidiMapper (plugin/include/MidiMapper.h) handles MIDI CC/note → target mapping with Learn, and lives in the processor (not the device layer) so the same map/learn/settings work identically in standalone and in DAW hosts; it serializes with plugin state via getStateInformation. Targets are four kinds: APVTS parameters, positional block powers (block1Power/rightBlock1Power — positional addressing is deliberate because block ids are ephemeral), stereo mode, and presetPrevious/presetNext steps. Behavior derivation: CC on a continuous parameter is absolute; CC on a toggle/trigger target fires once per press (value >= 64 fires, and a < 64 value also fires unless it follows a >= 64 from the same control — momentary release); note-on toggles continuous targets; program change n loads the nth preset in list order.

A block param field round-trips only if it exists in all FOUR state places: (1) getChainState in plugin/src/ProcessorChain.cpp (the BlockRow struct, the copyLane copy, AND params->setProperty('<field>',…) in serializeChain); (2) parseItem in plugin/ui/model/ChainState.cpp (item.<field> = num(v["params"], "<field>", default)); (3) updateBlockParam in plugin/src/ProcessorChain.cpp (the param == "<field>" branch); (4) ProcessorState.cpp (blockState.setProperty + getProperty restore). Missing any one = 'works sonically, snaps back to default on sync'. Two families sit in these four places: (a) CHAIN-LAYER dry-gain params — convDry, and reverbDry since the 2026-10-13 R1 pass — whose updateBlockParam branch does NOT call an engine setParams (the gain is applied in the chain's mix loop on the dry term only); (b) ENGINE params like reverbSharedMod (R2 shared Mod depth, 0..1 clamped), reverbWave (R2 Digital Shape, int 0..kNumWaves-1 clamped), and reverbLoCut (T-DAT-001, 0..1 clamped, stored fraction) — whose updateBlockParam branch stores the clamped value AND calls block->reverb.setParams(block->reverbParams()).

KnobScale (plugin/ui/core/KnobScale.h, port of knobScale.ts) keeps three domains separate: normalised 0..1 knob position, a DISPLAY unit (ms/dB/%/name) for the drag readout and type-in, and a STORAGE contract via toStored/fromStored that is what actually goes into the block param. knobToStored()/knobFromStored() fall back to toDisplay/fromDisplay when no explicit storage pair is declared — bit-identical legacy behaviour for real-unit-stored and identity-stored fraction knobs. Knobs whose stored domain is 0..1 but whose display unit is human (delayHeads 1..4 heads, compClip 0..2 raw depth behind a 0..200 % face, convGain ±24 dB, reverbDry ±24 dB, convPitch 0.25x..4x, spring lines 1..6) MUST declare toStored/fromStored or the tile writes the display unit into a 0..1 param, then the engine clamps it to 1.0, then the next resync snaps the knob back to max — the 2026-10-06 Heads glitch. T-DAT-001 additions: reverbSharedMod and reverbWave (R2) have NO custom scale (sharedMod is a plain 0..1 depth OFF at 0 by default; wave is an int 0..4 detent, identity-bound); the LoCut knob uses the loCutTaper() scale (KnobScale.h:792) with toStored(n) = 0.85 * pow(n, 0.7) (0..0.85 fraction for the mode-0 45 Hz HPF blend — never reaches 1.0; the 40-120 Hz absolute band-floor measured at full LoCut, user m03131 approved the 80% ceiling) with an inverse fromStored.

T-DAT-001 added a THIRD family member to the four-state-place rule: engine param reverbLoCut (0..1 clamped, default 0 = bit-pass). Its four places (line numbers as of the compressor reorg, commit 3ffb35b): (1) ChainBlock.h:409 field `double reverbLoCut = 0.0;` + the reverbParams() aggregate ending `reverbSharedMod, reverbWave, reverbLoCut` (reverbParams() at :423, aggregate end :433; matches Reverb::Params struct order) + ProcessorChain.cpp BlockRow init (:1204), row mirror (:1322), and params->setProperty("reverbLoCut", …) in serializeChain (:1500); (2) ChainState.cpp parseItem :230 `item.reverbLoCut = num(v["params"], "reverbLoCut", 0.0)`; (3) ProcessorChain.cpp isEffectParam list (:1939) + updateBlockParam branch (:2230-2231, jlimit 0..1 + block->reverb.setParams(block->reverbParams())); (4) ProcessorState.cpp blockState.setProperty (:283) + jlimit restore (:474).

The compressor TYPE axis added a fourth family member to the four-state-place rule: compType (int; per-mode sub-model within the compressor mode; 0 = the mode's own engine, the only type today — Compressor::numTypes(mode) returns 1 for every mode). Its four places: (1) ChainBlock.h:362 field `int compType = 0;` (immediately after compMode :361) + ProcessorChain.cpp BlockRow init (:1190), copyLane mirror row.compType = block->compType (:1291), and params->setProperty("compType", row.compType) in serializeChain (:1464); (2) ChainState.h:160 `int compType = 0;` on ChainItem + ChainState.cpp parseItem :190 `item.compType = num(v["params"], "compType", 0)`; (3) ProcessorChain.cpp param == "compType" in the isEffectParam list (:1939) + the else-if branch (:2123-2124) which stores the value VERBATIM (`block->compType = static_cast<int>(value)`) — no clamp here, the engine clamps via setParams (jlimit 0..numTypes-1) — and appends block->compType to the compressor setParams call site (:2128); (4) ProcessorState.cpp blockState.setProperty :232 + getProperty restore :384 (cast to int, verbatim). compType is the 11th and last field of the Compressor::Params aggregate, so every block->compressor.setParams({...}) call site (8 in ProcessorChain.cpp :2085-2146, 1 in ProcessorState.cpp :515) passes block->compType last.

The node-view (grid block interface) toggle is persisted as a UiPrefs key, not a block/chain param: UiPrefs::kNodeView = "t3k.nodeView" (UiPrefs.h:68), a plain getBool/setBool preference (default false = gallery view). The gallery|node toggle in PluginHeader (NodeViewToggle, a StereoModeToggle-style 80x36 two-segment control) reads it at construction via services_.prefs.getBool(UiPrefs::kNodeView, false) (PluginHeader.cpp:47) and fires onNodeViewToggle(nodeView) on click; PluginRoot writes the pref back with prefs.setBool and calls chainScreen().setView(nodeView) to swap the visible view.

The gallery/node view toggle is persisted as UiPrefs::kNodeView = "t3k.nodeView" (plugin/ui/services/UiPrefs.h:68); ChainScreen reads it at startup (getBool default false) and calls setView() to activate the node view, and the PluginHeader toggle writes it back on every click.

removeChainBlock persists intermediate empty slots (node-view batch 2, 2026-10-16): after pushing history it moves the block out and inserts a FRESH ChainBlock of type INSERT at the erased position (`it = chain.erase(it); chain.insert(it, std::make_unique<ChainBlock>(juce::Uuid()…, ChainBlockType::INSERT));`), so a mid-lane removal leaves the lane length unchanged with the gap in place; a subsequent addEffectBlock/landToneBlock into that index fills the gap in place instead of prepending. Inserts themselves are still not removable (the insert branch returns false). Covered by AddAtSlot.MidLaneGapIsFilledInPlace in test/src/add_at_slot_tests.cpp, which also re-baselined ChainBranchTest.AlignsBranchLaneEndWithTrunk (trunk stays at kMinLaneSlots=5 after removal; branch end 4→3).

ChainScreen::setView(false) sweeps the PluginRoot overlay layer with Popover::dismissAll: a strip mode/type menu is a Popover parented to the overlay, and hiding the strip only removes the ANCESTOR — the panel would ghost over the gallery (ComponentMovementWatcher fires only on the anchor's own visible-flag toggle, never on an ancestor's).
